choices.content: Yes, because \((\sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{3})^2=(\sqrt{5})^2\), and the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{5}\).

question.prompt: Is a triangle with side lengths \(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{3},\sqrt{5}\) a right triangle?

solutions.explanation: The longest side is \(\sqrt{5}\). Since \((\sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{3})^2=2+3=5=(\sqrt{5})^2\), the converse of the Pythagorean theorem applies. It is a right triangle with hypotenuse \(\sqrt{5}\).
solutions.title: Square the radical side lengths
